plan.diagnosis_summary: node_1's only fault is a metadata-like shortcut column export_shard_code (mi_norm 1.0002 locally vs 0.0034-0.0057 on peers, robust_z 49.7), which masked genuine localized label noise: with it excluded, node_1 shows 20.8% suspected noise and 12.4% high-confidence conflicts at mean self-confidence 0.457 versus node_3/node_4 baselines of 4.1-4.5% noise and 0.82 confidence. node_2's mild metric elevation (10.9% noise) is explained by legitimate Non-IID concentration of all four globally rare classes, and node_3 is fully healthy. node_4 has three recoverable schema-alias faults (timing columns matched by quantiles), a systematic 1/8 byte-unit drift (bit-vs-byte) confirmed by both benign anchors and conservation ratio 0.125, and 467 corrupted rows.

actions.evidence: mi_norm on node_1 = 1.0002 (exceeds label entropy 1.62512 nats) vs 0.0053/0.0034/0.0057 on node_2/3/4, robust_z 49.73: local shortcut artifact, not physical signal.

With export_shard_code excluded, node_1 shows suspected_noise_rate 0.2076, high_conf_conflict_rate 0.1238, mean_self_confidence 0.4568 and cv_macro_f1 0.4791 vs peer baselines 0.0409-0.0445, 0.0226-0.0241, 0.8175-0.8190 and 0.7144-0.7189.

Row health clean, conservation ratios 1.0, and CL metrics (noise 0.1086, confidence 0.6457) are attributable to legitimate Non-IID concentration of globally rare Analysis/Backdoor/Shellcode/Worms (100% share, 0.0 suspected rate) rather than corruption.

Schema unmapped column is only the dropped export_shard_code (mi_norm 0.0034), row health clean, all conservation ratios 1.0, and best CL baseline (noise 0.0445, confidence 0.8190); elevated sbytes/smean MI is shared by peers (robust_z 0.67-0.70).
